rationale: Parkinson mixed diet menu lists eggs and a composite motor outcome that includes speech. PubMed germinoma concerns unrelated speech disturbance. Exact EGG means electroglottography in one result, and two collection bodies remain inaccessible. No poached-egg speech intelligibility comparison was found.
Strain-defined fermented milk reports composite outcomes and yogurt serves as a diagnostic swallowing bolus in four reports. Those roles do not measure small handwriting after strained yogurt.
Rat activity declined during dried savory infusion exposure. Awake locomotion and the infused preparation leave fresh savory and clinical insomnia unresolved.
Spearmint extract work measures hits or reaction time. The PD intervention names unspecified mint on a mixed menu and reports no hand item or isolated dried spearmint intake.

Isolated eugenol gives pretreatment effects on mouse catalepsy but inconclusive post-treatment performance. Carolina or California allspice denotes another genus. Ground Pimenta dioica and felt or measured Parkinson rigidity remain untested in the reviewed sources.

Oral Sichuan pepper decoction shortened a mouse pole task after pre-exposure dosing. The related Japanese pepper experiment used a distilled intranasal preparation. Neither measured clinical bradykinesia after toasted pepper.

Cold-pressed oil studies use animal recognition tasks. A mixed ketogenic case lists avocado-oil mayonnaise with narrative executive change. Whole fruit and mixed menus have registered outcomes with no available executive estimate for the matched Preiss report. The data cannot assign a direction to the oil claim.

A Parkinson mixed menu allows canola oil and the motor disability scale includes handwriting, but preparation and item result are unavailable. The controlled clinical literature does not give a small-handwriting comparison by cold-pressed oil exposure.

A Parkinson lactulose and diet pilot permits green beans with no counts of falls. Original provider hits include agricultural studies, pressure falls, food preferences and isolated luteolin. Three exact original bodies remain open.
A prospective falls cohort groups bok choy with dark-green vegetables and does not separate cooking or the plant. The population and outcome differ from clinical Parkinson postural instability.

Animal extract work addresses evoked nociception. The two uncontrolled gout decoction reports have follow-up or count and score inconsistencies and unresolved independence. Both use boiled leaves and neither has a Parkinson comparison.
The dill-fruit survey and frozen-dill recall do not document individual hallucination events or frequency following fresh dill leaf exposure.

Rodent fennel extract studies vary by model and timing, with reduced, increased or inconclusive retention. No clinical postural stability comparison follows culinary toasted seed in the checked sources.
The dietary survey analyzes a composite mood and apathy outcome without a cayenne-specific coefficient or standalone apathy measure.

Flaxseed table oil has a small healthy-adult fluency difference and an inconclusive total frontal battery. A pooled omega-3 cohort has faster global cognitive decline without a separate oil estimate. A new executive-composite registry has no results. These measures and exposures leave the frozen comparison unresolved.
The 2022 and 2025 avocado-oil study family reports asymmetric turning in lesion-model rats, with pressing method unverified. Turning does not establish clinical dystonia direction.

A Parkinson bundled menu lists spinach with no preparation or facial-expression item result. Aged-rat conditioned eyeblink learning and a separate conference abstract about preferred omelets do not measure Parkinson facial expressiveness.

Two Parkinson mixed menus mention cucumber without a separate posture effect. Exact source bodies yield sea cucumber and unrelated gait or diagnostic matches. The lead-exposure rat extract paper gives no accessible assay name or arm estimates and cannot resolve effects of raw cucumber.

Several extracts improve movement proxies in toxin-exposed animals. Open-field exploration distance differs from walking velocity. No clinical walking-speed effect is isolated after dried culinary cilantro.

The Perilla eye trial uses aqueous extract with contradictory reported sample size and an ocular endpoint. Seed-peptide studies and athlete leaf-flavonoid results measure exercise performance. In the gastrectomy trial the registry and protocol disagree on perilla and have no fatigue results.
The Parkinson thesis uses a multi-ingredient honey mixture without a handwriting endpoint or ground anise dose. Rodent oil and motor-task context does not provide a clinical handwriting-size effect.
Isolated eugenol inhibited rat bladder strip contractions. Urgency frequency and oral ground clove were not evaluated.
In the cannabidiol study avocado oil was a common comparator basis and timed written symbols were counted, not measured for size. Food-oil refining and clinical micrographia were not measured.

The mixed Parkinson menu lists pumpkin seed oil with no separate rigidity item. Extract studies in a rodent catalepsy assay have variable results and differ in preparation. The inherited microarray body remains open after an original abstract review.
